proposedGroups.title: Hearing notice, contents, and witness testimony

proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Understand the notice and testimony rules that structure Discipline Committee hearings.

focusSelections.evidenceText:
8.2.4 .1 (a) Notice of Hearing as defined in
Schedule "A" section 15.1 shall be served at least
fourteen (14) days before the holding of the hearing,
upon the member whose conduct is being inquired
into and upon any other person or entity upon whom
the Discipline Committee deems it necessary for their
purpose to serve a Notice of Hearing upon.
(b) Notice of Hearing shall state the
subject matter of the hearing, the time and place of
the holding of the hearing and shall be signed by the
Registrar, or the Secretary of the Association of New
Brunswick Land Surveyors.
(c) The testimony of witnesses shall be
taken under oath or affirmation, which the chairman
of the Discipline Committee or any person
designated to do so on his behalf, is hereby
authorized to administer, and there shall be full right
to examine, cross - examine and re - examine
witnesses.

focusSelections.evidenceText:
8.2.4 .2 (d ) ( i ) The Chairman of the Discipline
Committee, or someone designated by him to act on
his behalf, and upon payment of the fees prescribed
in the Rules of Court, may issue a Summons to
Witness, in a form prescribed by Schedule"C"
Section 15.3, for the purpose of procuring the
attendance and evidence, verbal, documentary or
otherwise, of witnesses before the Committee by
signing the Summons to Witness and sealing it with
the seal of the Association.
( ii ) Pursuant to paragraph 8.2.4(d)(1),
the Registrar of the Association shall issue a blank
Summons to Witness signed by him under the seal of
the Association and the party may complete the
summons and insert therein of the required
particulars.
( iii ) A Summons to Witness shall be
served personally and service may be proved by
Affidavit.
( iv ) A Summons to Witness continues to
have effect until the conclusion of the hearing for
which the attendance of the witness is required.

This section defines professional misconduct through conduct contrary to public interest and ethics, breach of standards, and negligence or misrepresentation making a land surveyor unfit to practise, though a trailing awards heading appears in the source.

proposedGroups.title: Professional Misconduct definition
proposedGroups.reason: This section defines professional misconduct through conduct contrary to public interest and ethics, breach of standards, and negligence or misrepresentation making a land surveyor unfit to practise, though a trailing awards heading appears in the source.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Understand the by-law definition of Professional Misconduct.

focusSelections.evidenceText:
8.3.1 Professional Misconduct is defined as
follows:
(a) the conduct of a practitioner which, in the
opinion of the Discipline Committee, is detrimental
to the interests of the public and contravenes the
Canons of Ethics of the profession;
(b) the breach by a Land Surveyor of the
standards of surveying established by the
Association; and
(c) negligence, misrepresentation or any other
conduct which, in the opinion of the Discipline
Committee, renders a Land Surveyor unfit to practice
land surveying.
